statement: FKN (real constant number 3) is defined as the 'Normal penalty stiffness factor' in the summary of real constants table of the Contact Technology Guide.
The real constant list states that 'FKN (p. 49) defines a normal contact stiffness factor' for contact surface elements.
In Table 3.1 (Summary of Real Constant Defaults in Different Environments), FKN has real constant number 3 and an Ansys Mechanical APDL default value of 1.
In the same table, the Ansys Workbench default for FKN is 0.1, while the Ansys Mechanical APDL default is 1.

Section 3.9.4.2 states: 'For certain contact problems, you may choose to use the real constant FKN to define a normal contact stiffness factor. The usual factor range is from 0.1 - 10.0, with a default of 1.0.'
The default FKN value 'should work in most cases' according to section 3.9.4.2.
A negative value for FKN defines an absolute normal contact stiffness rather than a scaling factor.
For the penalty method (KEYOPT(2)=1), the spring stiffness is the contact stiffness, and the method uses real constants FKN and FKT for all values of KEYOPT(10).

A positive value for FKN is interpreted as a scaling factor and a negative value as an absolute value; contact-related settings (FTOLN, PINB, FKN, FKT, SLTO) are always averaged across all contact elements in a contact pair.

The program provides default values for contact stiffnesses (FKN, FKT), allowable penetration (FTOLN), and allowable slip (SLTO); material properties of underlying elements can affect the calculation of default contact stiffnesses.

The default contact normal stiffness is affected by defined material properties, element size, and the user-defined penetration tolerance (FTOLN); the default contact normal stiffness is inversely proportional to the final penetration tolerance.

When KEYOPT(10) = 0 or 2, the normal contact stiffness (used for the penalty method and the augmented Lagrange method) is updated at each iteration based on the current mean stress of the underlying elements and the allowable tolerance (FTOLN).
Generally, the contact stiffness FKN (and FKT) has units of FORCE/LENGTH3; for force-based models (CONTA175 KEYOPT(3)=0, CONTA177 KEYOPT(3)=0 or 4) the units are FORCE/LENGTH.
Ansys recommends using KEYOPT(10) = 0 or 2 to allow the program to update the contact stiffness automatically, and in most cases you do not need to define the contact stiffness.
In general, normal contact stiffness (FKN) has very little influence on the contact results when a Lagrange multiplier method is used; you should not overwrite the default FKN in most cases.

For the pressure-penetration exponential relationship, FKN can set a maximum cutoff stiffness: the actual cutoff stiffness is 1000 times the penalty stiffness input by the user or computed by the program (example: computed stiffness 42265 gives cutoff 0.42265E+08).
FKN can be defined as a function of primary variables (time, temperature, location, contact pressure, geometric penetration) by using tabular input (%tabname%) with R, RMORE, or RMODIF.
The user subroutine USERCNPROP.F is available for defining FKN by specifying the table name %_CNPROP% as the real constant value.
When the relaxation option is enabled (KEYOPT(11)=1 on the target element), FKN and FKT become translational and rotational relaxation coefficients rather than penalty stiffness factors.

When the contact element is used as part of a forced-distributed constraint and KEYOPT(7)=2 on the target element, FKN is used to define weighting factors in tabular format with node number as the primary variable.

For node-to-node contact (CONTA178) with the penalty or augmented Lagrange method, the program provides a default normal contact stiffness FKN based on Young's modulus E and the size of the underlying elements; FKN and FKS are factors, and absolute values require negative input.
For the shell-shell assembly penalty method with TARGE170 KEYOPT(5)=2, the contact stiffness for translational DOFs is input by real constant FKN or defaults to an internal value.

Many convergence failures in contact analyses are the result of using too large a value for contact stiffness (real constant FKN); if overpenetration occurs, a larger value of FKN is probably needed, and FKN can be changed between load steps via RMODIF.
FKN, FTOLN, PINB, and FKOP can be changed and can only be changed at the point of load step boundaries (contact stiffness may be redefined between load steps).
For the traction-based model, contact stiffness FKN has units FORCE/LENGTH for the force-based model but FORCE/LENGTH3 for the traction-based model.

The CNCHECK,AUTO command table lists FKN (No. 3, 'Normal penalty stiffness factor') as one of the real constants it implements, with behavior 'Cut in half if spurious contact is detected or contact searching is slow.'

KEYOPT(3)=1 for changing the units of FKN is valid only when a penalty-based algorithm is used (KEYOPT(2)=0 or 1) and the absolute normal contact stiffness value is explicitly specified (a negative value input for real constant FKN).
The GCDEF command example shows specifying contact stiffness FKN=10 at an interface by setting REALID to 14 and issuing the command R,14,,,10 (the 4th field of the R command is FKN).
The GCDEF example in the Contact Technology Guide defines a contact stiffness factor (FKN) of 10 at a specific contact interface via 'GCDEF,,SECT1,SECT2,,14' followed by 'R,14,,,10'.
RMODIF,GCN,3,10 defines a contact stiffness factor (FKN) of 10 for all real constant sets previously specified by GCDEF commands.
For general contact, Table 8.2 lists FKN (No. 3, 'Normal penalty stiffness factor') with default 1 for pair-based contact and 1 for general contact.
The Ansys Workbench product sets FKN = 10 for bonded contact and FKN = 1.0 for all other contact behaviors (FKN = 1 for all if bonded and other contact behavior coexist).
FKN and FKT are modified from near-zero to actual values by the program during the ramping of contact stiffness (ramping contact stiffness feature).

For debonding, the normal contact stiffness value is based on real constant FKN of the contact element; FKOP may be specified to decouple the gap (opening) stiffness from the penetration (closing) stiffness determined by FKN.

For the EMTGEN command (TRANS126 elements), the FKN argument is a contact stiffness factor used as a multiplier for a contact stiffness appropriate for bulk deformation, defaulting to 0.1 (this is a distinct FKN from the contact element real constant).
The technology showcase example script sets FKN with the comment 'Define FKN for real ID 100' via the command 'rmodif,100,3,1'.
The example table in the Technology Showcase lists FKN as a 'Structural stiffness' property with the example value '1.0 times underlying element stiffness'.

The Technology Showcase states 'Convergence of the problem is less sensitive to the normal contact stiffness factor (FKN) when using the surface-projection-based contact method (KEYOPT(4)=3)' and that 'FKN = 1 is optimal for nonlinear analysis'.

The demonstration guide similarly states convergence is less sensitive to FKN with surface-projection-based contact and that 'FKN = 1 is optimal for nonlinear analysis', with less iteration variation for smaller FKN values (0.1 to 1.0).
Example script td-17/impact_rigid.dat sets 'rmodif,2,3,-1e15 ! Specify FKN=1e15 (do not use for keyopt(2)=3)' to define an absolute normal contact stiffness by negative input.
Example script td-52/SequentialEmbankmentCase1.dat uses 'RMOD,2,3,10.0 ! Increase FKN' to raise the normal penalty stiffness factor to 10 for contact real constant set 2.
Example script td-7/cam_shaft_assembly.dat contains a commented-out line '!rmodif,3,3,1. ! FKN' showing FKN (real constant 3) set to the default factor 1.
Example script td-42/wirecrimp_fe.dat sets 'rmod,cid,3,0.1 ! FKN', lowering the normal penalty stiffness factor to 0.1 to ease convergence.
The Advanced Analysis Guide recommends lowering the contact stiffness by a factor of 10 (real constant FKN = 0.1 for the contact elements) to help semi-implicit solutions that fail during contact.
The Element Reference (TARGE169/170 KEYOPT(7)) states that for value 2, a user-defined weighting factor is used based on tabular input specified as real constant FKN.
The Element Reference states that when relaxation is enabled (KEYOPT(11)=1), the contact element real constants FKN and FKT are translational and rotational relaxation coefficients.

For the relaxation method, translational and rotational relaxation coefficients (similar to penalty stiffness for the contact penalty method) are specified through contact element real constants FKN and FKT respectively.
In bonded contact interface damping modeling, the first bonded contact pair represents interface damping along the normal direction (FKN used as a near-zero negative value with MP,DMPR).
